title: Quiet Please
paragraphs: Wyllis Cooper’s atmospheric anthology, usually narrated by Ernest Chappell, blends supernatural suspense, horror, fantasy, and psychological drama.

Wyllis Cooper atmospheric anthology built around original radio scripts, frequently first-person narration by featured actor Ernest Chappell, blending supernatural suspense, fantasy, horror and psychological drama.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual era (June 8, 1947 to September 13, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] and ABC era (September 19, 1948 to June 25, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Ernest Chappell (performer), Wyllis Cooper (director, writer, and host), Albert Buhrman (organist), Pat O'Malley (performer), Gene Parazzo (organist), Ed Latimer (performer), and Lotte Stavisky (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and [[org|org.e3a6b5feab2dd0c5|WJZ]].
The stories often return to death and mortality, supernatural and uncanny phenomena, time and temporal dislocation, war and military aftermath, ghosts and the dead, and memory and identity.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Original writing for the radio medium, Mutual-to-ABC network transition, and Wyllis Cooper horror-radio lineage.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]].
